apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: deploy-host
  title: System deployment manifests (shared)
  description: The Dapr components a system's blocks share, as one ArgoCD Application.
  tags: [deploy, gitops, kustomize, dapr]
  labels:
    intropy.dev/template-kind: deploy
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    # domain is optional, deliberately: it is only a GitOps path segment, no
    # skeleton references it outside component.yaml (repo metadata a local render
    # never emits), and a local render has no domain.
    required: [system, namespace]
    properties:
      domain:
        type: string
        title: Domain
        description: Business domain the system belongs to, as a GitOps path segment. Not required — a local render has no domain, and no skeleton references it outside component.yaml, which local rendering never emits.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      system:
        type: string
        title: System
        description: System name, as a GitOps path segment.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespace:
        type: string
        title: Namespace
        description: The Kubernetes namespace the system's blocks run in. With namespacePerEnv the environment is prefixed to it.
        default: integrations
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespacePerEnv:
        type: boolean
        title: Namespace per environment
        description: Prefix the environment to the namespace, e.g. test-acme-integrations. Leave false for a single flat namespace.
        default: false
      pubsub:
        type: string
        title: Pub/sub broker
        description: The Dapr pub/sub building block to declare, from deploy.yaml platform.pubsub. rabbitmq is what local rendering uses.
        enum: [in-memory, rabbitmq, servicebus]
        default: rabbitmq
      pubsubName:
        type: string
        title: Pub/sub component name
        description: The name blocks resolve the broker by. Must match what the generated C# uses.
        default: pubsub
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
  values:
    secretName: "{{ .system }}-secrets"

  # Which files exist at all, rather than only what is in them. First match
  # decides; a path no rule matches is always included.
  files:
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-in-memory.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "in-memory" }}'
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-rabbitmq.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "rabbitmq" }}'
    - path: base/dapr/pubsub-servicebus.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .pubsub "servicebus" }}'

    # The generic environment overlay never renders for the local environment:
    # it would set a namespace line, while the local overlay stays
    # namespace-agnostic (local rendering sets the namespace on the root
    # kustomization it writes). A dedicated overlays/local/ skeleton carries
    # that thin-but-namespaceless variant. local is reserved — no customer
    # environment may be named that.
    - path: 'overlays/{{ .env }}/**'
      when: '{{ ne .env "local" }}'

    # No external connectors means no bindings, and an empty multi-doc file in a
    # kustomize resources list breaks the build. Never for the local environment:
    # the fixture catalog on deploy-component carries the local bindings, and a
    # REPLACE-ME scaffold here would duplicate every Component the fixtures
    # render.
    - path: base/bindings/**
      when: '{{ and (gt (len .topology.connectors) 0) (ne .env "local") }}'

apiVersion: intropy.dev/v1
kind: Template
metadata:
  name: deploy-component
  title: Block deployment manifests
  description: The workload and overlays for one block, as one ArgoCD Application.
  tags: [deploy, gitops, kustomize]
  labels:
    intropy.dev/template-kind: deploy
spec:
  parameters:
    type: object
    # domain is optional, deliberately: it is only a GitOps path segment, no
    # skeleton references it, and a local render has no domain. GitOps creation
    # derives it from the destination or requires --domain.
    required: [name, system, registry]
    properties:
      name:
        type: string
        title: Component
        description: Block name, as a GitOps path segment.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      domain:
        type: string
        title: Domain
        description: Only a GitOps path segment; no skeleton file references it.
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      system:
        type: string
        title: System
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      appId:
        type: string
        title: Dapr app-id
        description: The identity the sidecar registers as, and what a Component's scopes list.
      kind:
        type: string
        title: Block kind
        description: The topology's block kind, carried through as a label.
        default: ""
      workload:
        type: string
        title: Workload
        description: An extractor is scheduled and exits; everything else stays resident.
        enum: [cronjob, deployment]
        default: deployment
      namespace:
        type: string
        title: Namespace
        default: integrations
        pattern: "^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$"
      namespacePerEnv:
        type: boolean
        title: Namespace per environment
        default: false
      registry:
        type: string
        title: Registry
        description: The registry from deploy.yaml.
      imageNamespace:
        type: string
        title: Image namespace
        description: The path segment between the registry and the image name. Must match what CI pushes.
        default: integrations
      replicas:
        type: integer
        title: Replicas
        default: 1
      sourceDir:
        type: string
        title: Source directory
        description: The block's directory in the source repository, used for component.yaml sourcePaths. Empty when no scaffold record was found.
        default: ""
  # The closed fixture catalog for the local development cluster: one Dapr
  # binding skeleton per fixture type in overlays/local/fixtures/, switched on
  # the connector's binding for this render. Local manifest rendering fails a
  # release that ships a local overlay without this list and validates explicit
  # or interactive choices against it. Adding a fixture is a skeleton file, an
  # entry here, and the fixture server in the k3s setup scripts — a template PR,
  # not a CLI release.
  local:
    fixtures: [sftp, smb, http, file]

  values:
    imageRepo: "{{ .registry }}/{{ .imageNamespace }}/{{ .name }}"
    # Never a real tag. `intropy deploy pin` writes the digest; a tag here would let
    # what runs change without a deployment, which is the whole thing this
    # toolchain exists to prevent.
    imageTag: "unpinned"

  files:
    # The CronJob's schedule is deployment configuration that differs between
    # the local cluster (a dev cadence, applied unreviewed) and every other
    # environment (a REPLACE-ME a human fills in), and .env may only vary
    # under overlays/ — so the variant is picked here, per file, and
    # base/kustomization.yaml names the picked file. First match decides.
    - path: base/cronjob.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ and (eq .workload "cronjob") (ne .env "local") }}'
    - path: base/cronjob-local.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ and (eq .workload "cronjob") (eq .env "local") }}'
    - path: base/deployment.yaml.tmpl
      when: '{{ eq .workload "deployment" }}'

    # The generic environment overlay never renders for the local environment:
    # it and overlays/local/ would both land at overlays/local/, and the walk
    # order ("local" sorts before "{{ .env }}") means the thin overlay would
    # silently overwrite the fixture-carrying one. local is reserved for the
    # local overlay — no customer environment may be named that.
    - path: 'overlays/{{ .env }}/**'
      when: '{{ ne .env "local" }}'

# intropy-dev-env

Curated ephemeral dev environment for Intropy tooling services
(idempotency-service, business-incident-service) on a local k3d cluster.

Everything is disposable: `./down.sh` deletes the cluster and every byte
of state with it.

## Prerequisites

- Docker Desktop (running)
- `k3d`, `kubectl`, `helm`, `dapr` CLI (`brew install k3d kubectl helm dapr/tap/dapr-cli`)
- The service repos checked out as siblings of this repo:
  - `../idempotency-service`
  - `../business-incident-service`

## Usage

```bash
./up.sh       # create cluster, install Dapr + RabbitMQ, build images, install services
./status.sh   # pods and helm releases at a glance
./down.sh     # delete the cluster; nothing persists
```

`up.sh` is idempotent — re-run it after fixing a failure and it converges.

## What gets installed

| Component | Where | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| k3d cluster `intropy` | Docker | single-node, config in `clusters/k3d.yaml` |
| Dapr control plane | `dapr-system` | `dapr init -k` |
| RabbitMQ | `fixtures` ns | `guest:guest`, non-persistent, matches template connection string |

**The image reference is pinned to a bare name.** `deployment.yaml` and

any built Deployment image has no tag, as a second net.

**The fixture bindings live here.** `overlays/local/fixtures/` carries one

Short answer: **no, not as-is.** It would apply cleanly (the YAML is valid and `kubectl apply` would succeed), but the pods wouldn't come up healthy. Three concrete gaps:

## 1. Images won't resolve

The render rewrites every Deployment image to `<component>:dev`, expecting that exact tag side-loaded into the cluster. The dev env's `images/build.sh` builds `local/idempotency-service:0.1.0`, `local/business-incident-service:1.0.8` — different names, different tags. You'd get `ImagePullBackOff`.

Workaround exists: `--image <component>=local/business-incident-service:1.0.8` per component. That part of the CLI works today.

## 2. Fixture bindings point at servers that don't exist there

The rendered local overlay's fixture contract assumes the *int local* k3s setup, not this dev env:

| Fixture in template | Dev env reality |
|---|---|
| `sftp.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:22`, `intropy`/`intropy` | Service is `sftpgo`, SFTP on **2022**, user `sftpgo`/`sftpgo` |
| `smb.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:445` | Nothing installed |
| `http.fixtures.svc.cluster.local:8080` | Nothing installed |
| (no `s3`/`blob` fixture in catalog) | Garage + `fixtures-blob` binding exist, but the template catalog can't emit one |

Any connector you bind to `sftp`/`smb`/`http` renders a Dapr Component pointing at a nonexistent Service — the sidecar logs component load failures and the binding fails at runtime. Only `file` (container-local) and the RabbitMQ pub/sub actually resolve.

## 3. No state stores, no databases

The deploy-host template renders **only** pub/sub and bindings. The dev env services get PostgreSQL (helm subchart) and their Dapr state store components from their own charts. A rendered manifest set has neither — so a service needing a state store starts with a sidecar that can't initialize it.

There's also a duplication hazard: applying rendered manifests for `business-incident-service` into the same cluster where `up.sh` already helm-installed it gives you two deployments of the same app, possibly fighting over the same Dapr app-id.
